title: A heterogeneously integrated coupled-cavity frequency beam splitter
authors: Lucas M. Cohen, Manuel H. Muñoz-Arias, Mohan Sarovar, Nicholas A. Boynton, Shawn C. Arterburn, Thomas A. Friedmann, Nils T. Otterstrom, Paul S. Davids, Michael Gehl
abstract: Frequency encoded photonic qubits promise a scalable path towards high-dimensional quantum information processing, but require efficient components for coherently mixing frequency modes. Coupled cavity modulators provide this functionality by using only a single driving microwave tone to couple hybridized optical supermodes. Here, we demonstrate a heterogeneously integrated thin-film lithium-niobate-on-silicon coupled-cavity modulator that realizes tunable bidirectional frequency mode transformations, including \(50/50\) beam splitting and near complete frequency swapping with \(>20~\mathrm{dB}\) pump extinction at a \(10~\mathrm{GHz}\) supermode splitting. Because the electro-optic film is bonded onto a foundry fabricated silicon photonics platform, the approach is compatible with co-integration of photon pair sources, spectral filters, active tuning elements, and single photon detectors. We also bond thin-film lithium tantalate onto the same coupled-cavity platform, demonstrating material flexibility for scalable integrated frequency bin quantum photonic circuits.
summary: This paper reports the successful demonstration of a heterogeneously integrated coupled-cavity modulator using thin-film lithium niobate on a silicon platform. The device achieves tunable frequency-mode transformations, such as 50/50 beam splitting, essential for building integrated quantum photonic circuits. This work showcases a scalable, foundry-compatible approach for quantum information processing hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for efficient components to coherently mix frequency modes for frequency-encoded photonic qubits, which is crucial for scalable high-dimensional quantum information processing.
main_result: They demonstrated a heterogeneously integrated coupled-cavity modulator capable of tunable bidirectional frequency-mode transformations, including 50/50 beam splitting and near-complete frequency swapping.
method: The experiment involves fabricating and characterizing a coupled-cavity modulator by bonding thin-film lithium niobate onto a silicon photonics platform and driving it with both optical and microwave signals.
model_or_system: The system is a coupled-cavity modulator built on a silicon photonics platform using thin-film lithium niobate. It functions by coupling hybridized optical supermodes using a microwave drive, allowing for controlled frequency transformations.
key_observables: Transmission spectra, power extinction ratios (e.g., >20 dB pump extinction), and the realization of specific beam-splitting ratios (e.g., 50/50).
important_parameters: Supermode splitting (10 GHz), coupling rates ($\kappa_e, \kappa_i$), and the electro-optic modulation strength ($V_\pi L$).
main_assumptions: The approach assumes compatibility with foundry-fabricated silicon photonics platforms and the ability to bond high-quality electro-optic films like TFLN.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the heterogeneous Si/TFLN platform fabrication process flow, and subsequent figures show characterization results like avoided mode crossings and frequency conversion spectra.
paper_structure: The paper details the physical system design, presents the fabrication process flow, and then reports experimental characterization results showing the device's ability to perform frequency beam splitting and shifting.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly practical, integrated platform for quantum light manipulation, directly addressing hardware bottlenecks in scalable quantum communication and computation.
